Mount & Blade: Warband. You can do fucking anything. In my current game(In th Gekokujo mod that replaces the map with Japan) I was trying to get in good with my faction by getting married. I learned poems, dedicated tournaments, payed a 9000 gold dowry, the whole 9(000) yards. However, my advances offended a fellow vassal: Lord Ishiki. He hated me because he was trying to marry her too. The final straw was when she fell in love with me and we married. So, we silently loathed eachother.

Then, I had my chance at something huge: Capturing a castle by myself. I moved in with my army. It consists of 90 men, but they're all top tier units. Luckily, the enemy force simply surrendered in exchange for being allowed to all live. Of course, I requested that my new victory be awarded to me. I rode around and defeated enemy armies before they could join together to defeat my army and stocked up my garrison. Finally, roughly a week after my victory, a letter arrives addressed to me from the Great Lord Ukita himself. As I read through the traditional congratulations, I excitedly rush through to get to the announcement that I would receive the castle. I read down, and it says "However, I have decided to award the castle to...Lord Ishiki." Should it have been any other man, I wouldn't be angered. But to see him throw away my victory with only the compensation of 700 gold digusted me. I refuses to accept. I took the castle and declared my own empire.

Now, with only a castle and a town, I'm fighting an empire. Sadly, my army simply isn't big enough to conquer their castles and cities. I've taken half of the enemy lords prisoner(But that slippery devil Lord Ishiki escaped from our fight like a coward). Now, I can't lose or win. My strategy is just to invest all my points in charisma and leadership to build up my army. That's just one of the many scenarios I've had in Mount & Blade. The actual gameplay is an isometric overworld map where you move around, with battles being in thrid person while you command your army. It's got some RPG elements with a bunh of skills and stats. I can't reccomend this amazing game enough.
